answer: A radiometric protocol limits Sybil attacks by binding agent identities to real-time solar irradiance telemetry. Nodes prove physical presence by contrasting ambient sunlight in an orchard or near a glacier against a local velvet light-trap baseline. An adversary must incur substantial hardware and deployment costs maintaining discrete photometers per identity. However, localized cloud cover can distort irradiance levels, erroneously rejecting valid participants.
